title: Ask the Board of Zoning Appeals for a variance, or appeal a zoning decision
question: I need a variance, or I disagree with a zoning administrator's decision in Albemarle County. How do I go to the Board of Zoning Appeals, and what are the deadlines?
office: Albemarle County Board of Zoning Appeals (five members appointed by the Circuit Court); applications and appeals are filed through the Community Development Department (Zoning Administrator)
summary: Albemarle's Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA) decides variances and appeals of zoning decisions. A variance relaxes a lot-size, setback, height or similar rule when a physical condition of the property makes it unreasonable; it cannot change the use, and the applicant must prove each state-law test. Apply in Civic Access with a written justification, plat or survey and drawings by the filing deadline, eight to ten weeks before a meeting; the fee is $590 plus a 4% technology surcharge, and probably a notice charge ($235 plus postage and advertising). Fees change on January 1, 2027. Appeal a Zoning Administrator's written decision or violation notice within 30 days (10 for some temporary uses); the fee is $350. The BZA must decide within 90 days. Court review: petition the Albemarle Circuit Court within 30 days.

legal_basis.quote: Every locality that has enacted or enacts a zoning ordinance pursuant to this chapter or prior enabling laws shall establish a board of zoning appeals
shall establish a board of zoning appeals that shall consist of either five or seven residents of the locality
the board shall offer an equal amount of time in a hearing on the case to the applicant, appellant or other person aggrieved under § 15.2-2314 , and the staff of the local governing body
The applicant, landowner or his agent or attorney may have ex parte communications with a member of the board prior to the hearing but may not discuss the facts or law relative to a particular case.

If any ex parte discussion of facts or law in fact occurs, the party engaging in such communication shall inform the other party as soon as practicable and advise the other party of the substance of such communication.

shall be made available without cost to such applicant, appellant or other person aggrieved under § 15.2-2314 , as soon as practicable thereafter, but in no event more than three business days of providing such materials to a member of the board

To hear and decide appeals from any order, requirement, decision, or determination made by an administrative officer in the administration or enforcement of this article or of any ordinance adopted pursuant thereto.
The determination of the administrative officer shall be presumed to be correct.

At a hearing on an appeal, the administrative officer shall explain the basis for his determination after which the appellant has the burden of proof to rebut such presumption of correctness by a preponderance of the evidence.
Altering the order of evidence is a reversible error only if the appellant lodges an objection citing this section and the board subsequently refuses to reorder the hearing.

the burden of proof shall be on the applicant for a variance to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that his application meets the standard for a variance as defined in § 15.2-2201 and the criteria set out in this section
a variance shall be granted if the evidence shows that the strict application of the terms of the ordinance would unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property
the property interest for which the variance is being requested was acquired in good faith and any hardship was not created by the applicant for the variance
the granting of the variance will not be of substantial detriment to adjacent property and nearby properties in the proximity of that geographical area

the condition or situation of the property concerned is not of so general or recurring a nature as to make reasonably practicable the formulation of a general regulation to be adopted as an amendment to the ordinance
the granting of the variance does not result in a use that is not otherwise permitted on such property or a change in the zoning classification of the property

the relief or remedy sought by the variance application is not available through a special exception process that is authorized in the ordinance pursuant to subdivision 6 of § 15.2-2309 or the process for modification of a zoning ordinance pursuant to subdivision A 4 of § 15.2-2286 at the time of the filing of the variance application
such request shall be granted by the locality unless a variance from the board of zoning appeals under this section is required in order for such request to be granted
No variance shall be considered except after notice and hearing as required by § 15.2-2204 .
the board may give such notice by first-class mail rather than by registered or certified mail
In granting a variance, the board may impose such conditions regarding the location, character, and other features of the proposed structure or use as it may deem necessary in the public interest
the property upon which a property owner has been granted a variance shall be treated as conforming for all purposes under state law and local ordinance
the structure permitted by the variance may not be expanded unless the expansion is within an area of the site or part of the structure for which no variance is required under the ordinance
To hear and decide appeals from the decision of the zoning administrator after notice and hearing as provided by § 15.2-2204 .

No provision of this section shall be construed as granting any board the power to rezone property or to base board decisions on the merits of the purpose and intent of local ordinances duly adopted by the governing body.

"Variance" means, in the application of a zoning ordinance, a reasonable deviation from those provisions regulating the shape, size, or area of a lot or parcel of land or the size, height, area, bulk, or location of a building or structure when the strict application of the ordinance would unreasonably restrict the utilization of the property
It shall not include a change in use, which change shall be accomplished by a rezoning or by a conditional zoning.
and such need for a variance would not be shared generally by other properties, and provided such variance is not contrary to the purpose of the ordinance
Applications for special exceptions and variances may be made by any property owner, tenant, government official, department, board or bureau.
Applications shall be made to the zoning administrator in accordance with rules adopted by the board.
The application and accompanying maps, plans or other information shall be transmitted promptly to the secretary of the board who shall place the matter on the docket to be acted upon by the board.
The zoning administrator shall also transmit a copy of the application to the local planning commission which may send a recommendation to the board or appear as a party at the hearing.
Any locality may provide by ordinance that substantially the same application will not be considered by the board within a specified period, not exceeding one year.
An appeal to the board may be taken by any person aggrieved or by any officer, department, board or bureau of the locality affected by any decision of the zoning administrator

shall include a statement informing the recipient that he may have a right to appeal the notice of a zoning violation or a written order within 30 days in accordance with this section, and that the decision shall be final and unappealable if not appealed within 30 days
The zoning violation or written order shall include the applicable appeal fee and a reference to where additional information may be obtained regarding the filing of an appeal.

The appeal period shall not commence until the statement is given and the zoning administrator's written order is sent by registered or certified mail with proof of delivery to, or posted at, the last known address or usual place of abode of the property owner or its registered agent, if any.
The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.
The zoning administrator shall forthwith transmit to the board all the papers constituting the record upon which the action appealed from was taken.
The fee for filing an appeal shall not exceed the costs of advertising the appeal for public hearing and reasonable costs.
any such civil penalty shall not be assessed by a court having jurisdiction during the pendency of the 30-day appeal period

An appeal shall stay all proceedings in furtherance of the action appealed from unless the zoning administrator certifies to the board that by reason of facts stated in the certificate a stay would in his opinion cause imminent peril to life or property

after 60 days have elapsed from the date of the written order, requirement, decision or determination where the person aggrieved has materially changed his position in good faith reliance on the action of the zoning administrator or other administrative officer
if the board's attempt to reach a decision results in a tie vote, the matter may be carried over until the next scheduled meeting at the request of the person filing the appeal

The concurring vote of a majority of the membership of the board shall be necessary to reverse any order, requirement, decision or determination of an administrative officer or to decide in favor of the applicant on any matter upon which it is required to pass under the ordinance or to effect any variance from the ordinance.
The board shall keep minutes of its proceedings and other official actions which shall be filed in the office of the board and shall be public records.

has been published twice in some newspaper published or having general circulation in the locality, with the first notice appearing no more than 28 days before and the second notice appearing no less than five days before the date of the meeting referenced in the notice

steps.step: Variance: check that a variance is the right request
steps.who: Property owner, tenant or their agent
steps.how: A variance relaxes a rule about the shape, size or area of a lot, or the size, height, bulk or location of a building (for example a setback or a minimum lot size), when a physical condition of the property makes the rule unreasonable. It cannot allow a use the zoning district does not permit or change the zoning; that takes a rezoning, a special use permit or a text amendment through the Board of Supervisors. State law also bars a variance when the relief is available through a special exception process authorized under Va. Code § 15.2-2309(6), or through a zoning administrator modification under § 15.2-2286(A)(4). The County calls its own special exceptions, variations and waivers a different process from a variance: they waive or modify a rule only where that section of the ordinance allows it, and a zoning special exception needs Board of Supervisors approval. Ask Community Development whether the relief you need is available that way (see caveats). An appeal, not a variance, is the route when you think the Zoning Administrator read the ordinance wrongly (steps s13 to s18).

steps.step: Variance: ask Community Development about the property before applying (optional)
steps.how: Send the property address or parcel ID with the question, and any plat or plan, to cddinquiry@albemarle.org, leave a voicemail on the CDD Inquiry Line (434-296-5832 extension 3440), or file a general inquiry in Civic Access (an account is needed). Staff confirm the inquiry and give a time frame for the answer.
steps.deadline: Staff confirm within 24-48 hours, as the County page states

steps.step: Variance: prepare the application and the written justification
steps.who: Applicant (any property owner, tenant, government official, department, board or bureau may apply)
steps.how: The County checklist requires: the completed application; a written explanation of what is asked, with the evidence that supports the variance; copies of plans or other information; a copy of a recorded plat or boundary survey; and drawings of all existing and proposed improvements. The applicant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the request meets the state definition of a variance (a reasonable deviation, a need not shared generally by other properties, and not contrary to the purpose of the ordinance; Va. Code § 15.2-2201) and the state tests: the rule unreasonably restricts use of the property (or the variance relieves a hardship from a physical condition, or is a reasonable modification for a person with a disability); the property was bought in good faith and the hardship was not self-created; no substantial detriment to nearby property; the condition is not so general that the ordinance should be amended instead; no change of use or zoning; and the relief is not available by special exception or zoning administrator modification. Address each point with evidence.

steps.step: If you are not the owner: give the owner notice of the application and certify it
steps.who: Applicant who is not the record owner (for example a tenant or contract buyer)
steps.how: State law puts this notice on the Zoning Administrator, who may instead direct the applicant to give it and to show satisfactory evidence that it was given; the County form is that evidence. Hand-deliver or mail a copy of the application to the record owner (the address on the current real estate tax records is enough) and file the County's Certification That Notice of the Application Has Been Provided to the Landowner with the application. The County form names determinations and appeals among the applications it covers; ask Community Development whether it wants the form with a variance application too (see caveats).
steps.deadline: State law requires written notice to the owner within 10 days of the receipt of the request (Va. Code § 15.2-2204(H))

steps.step: Variance: file the application in Civic Access by the BZA filing deadline
steps.how: Apply online in the County's Civic Access portal (registration required) under the Variance application type, uploading the checklist documents. Filing deadlines are Mondays at 3 P.M., eight to ten weeks before each BZA meeting. The remaining deadlines in the 2026 schedule are Nov 02, 2026 for the Jan 05, 2027 meeting, Nov 30, 2026 for Feb 02, 2027, Jan 04, 2027 for Mar 02, 2027, and Feb 01, 2027 for Apr 06, 2027 (2027 dates are tentative; the Oct 05, 2026 deadline for the Dec 01, 2026 meeting has passed). Track the application and staff comments in Civic Access once you have an application number.
steps.deadline: The 2026 Submission and Review Schedule's 'Deadline for Filing (3 P.M.)' (a Monday) for the chosen meeting
steps.fee: $590 (BZA - Variance and Special Use Permit, fee page of 2026-08; revised fees take effect January 1, 2027), plus the 4% technology surcharge; the Required Notice fee ($235 base at application plus actual postage and advertising) is listed in the zoning fee table and likely applies (see caveats)

steps.how: Pay through the Civic Access payment portal linked from the County page (the link opens the portal's invoice-payment page; the County pages do not say how or when the amount due is issued, so ask Community Development if you have not received it). If the Required Notice charge applies (see caveats), it is a $235 base fee at application, plus what the required postage and newspaper advertising once it is known.
steps.deadline: If the Required Notice charge applies, its $235 base fee is due at the time of application, per the fee schedule

steps.step: The Zoning Administrator sends the file to the BZA and the Planning Commission
steps.how: Staff review the application, send it to the BZA's secretary to be docketed for a hearing, and send a copy to the Planning Commission, which may send a recommendation or take part as a party.
steps.quote: The application and accompanying maps, plans or other information shall be transmitted promptly to the secretary of the board who shall place the matter on the docket to be acted upon by the board.

steps.how: Staff mail notice to the owners of abutting parcels, as the County page says (Va. Code § 15.2-2309(2) also refers to property immediately across the street or road, and allows first-class mail instead of registered or certified mail), and publish it in the newspaper twice, on the two Thursday advertisement dates in the BZA schedule. A public notice sign is also posted on the property for variances and appeals; current signs are listed on the County's Public Notice Signs dashboard.
steps.deadline: Newspaper notice twice: the first no more than 28 days and the second no less than five days before the hearing (Va. Code § 15.2-2204(A)); the schedule lists the two Thursday advertisement dates for each meeting
steps.fee: Postage and advertising are charged to the applicant (Required Notice fee)

steps.step: Staff report; your right to see what the BZA members get
steps.how: Staff write a report and recommendation for the BZA. Any materials about the case given to a BZA member, including a staff recommendation or report, must be made available without cost to the applicant or appellant (and any other person aggrieved under Va. Code § 15.2-2314). Before the hearing you may communicate with BZA members, but you may not discuss the facts or law of the case; if such a discussion does happen, the party who had it must tell the other party as soon as practicable and say what was discussed. Ask for other County documents with a Virginia FOIA request.
steps.deadline: No more than three business days after the materials go to a BZA member (Va. Code § 15.2-2308.1(B))
steps.quote: shall be made available without cost to such applicant, appellant or other person aggrieved under § 15.2-2314 , as soon as practicable thereafter, but in no event more than three business days of providing such materials to a member of the board

steps.how: Contact Community Development before the meeting to arrange any presentation, and bring copies of any handouts for the Recording Clerk. Stay on the questions in the application or on staff's determination; the BZA cannot change County ordinances. Either side may ask the BZA to defer a hearing, orally or in writing, with reasons.

steps.who: Board of Zoning Appeals; County staff; applicant or appellant; members of the public
steps.how: meets in person on each month's first Tuesday at 2 p.m. in Lane Auditorium, County Office Building, 401 McIntire Road, when cases are scheduled (check the schedule; for example the November 2026 meeting is on Nov 10). Staff present the report, then the applicant or appellant speaks (15 minutes, plus 5 minutes of rebuttal, with equal time for staff); each member of the public gets one turn of up to 3 minutes; then the hearing closes.

The BZA votes by roll call. Granting a variance takes at least three affirmative votes (a majority of the five-member board). A tie vote defeats the motion, and the defeat of a motion to deny is not an approval (BZA Rules 5(D) and 5(E)). The BZA may attach conditions and require a bond. A property granted a variance is treated as conforming, but the varied structure cannot be expanded into an area that needs a variance without a new one. Then apply for the building permit or zoning clearance the project needs. The decision date is the date of the final vote.
steps.deadline: Within ninety days of the filing of the application (Va. Code § 15.2-2312)

steps.step: Appeal: get the zoning decision in writing
steps.who: Property owner or other person affected; Zoning Administrator
steps.how: An appeal is taken from any order, requirement, decision or ruling of the Zoning Administrator or another administrative officer, such as a notice of violation or an Official Letter of Determination. Getting the decision in writing gives a clear date to count the appeal period from, and the 60-day protection in Va. Code § 15.2-2311(C) covers only written decisions. To get a formal ruling (for example on development rights, vested rights, parcels of record, nonconformities or how a use is classified), file the Official Letter of Determination Application in Civic Access. A notice of violation or written order must state the right to appeal within 30 days, the appeal fee and where to get more information.
steps.deadline: The County says letters may take up to 90 days; state law requires a response within 90 days of the request unless the requester agrees to longer (Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4))
steps.fee: $220 (Zoning Determination, fee page of 2026-08; revised fees take effect January 1, 2027), plus the 4% technology surcharge

steps.step: Appeal: work out the appeal deadline
steps.how: Count 30 days from the decision (the day of the decision is not counted; if the last day falls when the office is closed, file the next business day). Decisions about temporary or seasonal commercial uses have a 10-day appeal period. For a notice of violation or written order, the period starts only after the notice states the appeal right and is sent by registered or certified mail with proof of delivery to, or posted at, the owner's last known address. A decision not appealed in time becomes final and unappealable.
steps.deadline: 30 days (10 days for decisions on temporary or seasonal commercial uses)

steps.step: Appeal: file the notice of appeal
steps.who: Any person aggrieved, or a County officer, department, board or bureau affected by the decision
steps.how: File the 'Appeal of Zoning Administrator’s Determination' application in Civic Access, stating the grounds of the appeal (state law requires the notice of appeal to be filed with the Zoning Administrator and with the BZA). If you are not the owner, include the owner-notice certification (step s4). Appeals do not follow the variance filing calendar; they go to the next appropriate meeting after filing.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days after the decision appealed from (10 days for temporary or seasonal commercial uses)
steps.fee: $350 (Appeal – Board of Zoning Appeals, fee page of 2026-08; revised fees take effect January 1, 2027), plus the 4% technology surcharge; state law caps the appeal fee at advertising and reasonable costs
steps.quote: The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

steps.step: Appeal: the record goes to the BZA and enforcement is paused
steps.how: The Zoning Administrator sends the BZA the papers behind the decision. The appeal stays enforcement unless the Zoning Administrator certifies that a stay would cause imminent peril to life or property; then only a restraining order from the BZA or a court can stop it. Courts may not assess zoning civil penalties during the 30-day appeal period. The appeal is put on the next suitable meeting after it is filed and heard after notice under Va. Code §§ 15.2-2204 and 15.2-2309(3), as for a variance (step s8); the County's Public Notice Signs page lists appeals among the hearings it posts signs for.

steps.who: Board of Zoning Appeals; Zoning Administrator; appellant
steps.how: At the hearing the Zoning Administrator explains the decision first. The decision is presumed correct, and the appellant must rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence. The BZA decides whether the administrator was correct, applying the ordinances, laws and regulations; it cannot rezone or judge whether the ordinance is wise. If the BZA changes that order of evidence, object at the hearing and cite Va. Code § 15.2-2309: changing the order is reversible error only if the appellant objects and the BZA refuses to reorder the hearing. Time limits are as in step s11.
steps.quote: At a hearing on an appeal, the administrative officer shall explain the basis for his determination after which the appellant has the burden of proof to rebut such presumption of correctness by a preponderance of the evidence.

steps.how: The BZA may affirm, reverse or modify the decision in whole or in part. Reversing takes at least three affirmative votes. On a tie vote the appellant may ask to carry the appeal over to the next scheduled meeting. The decision date is the date of the final vote on the merits, and the BZA's minutes are public records.
steps.deadline: Within ninety days of the filing of the appeal (Va. Code § 15.2-2312)

escalation.quote: if the board's attempt to reach a decision results in a tie vote, the matter may be carried over until the next scheduled meeting at the request of the person filing the appeal

escalation.next: A Virginia Freedom of Information Act request to the County
escalation.quote: such request shall be made pursuant to § 2.2-3704

escalation.trigger: The variance is denied or the appeal is lost, and there is new evidence that could not be presented at the hearing, or conditions have changed
escalation.next: Board of Zoning Appeals rehearing (written application; the motion needs three affirmative votes and can be granted only if the decision has not already been appealed to the Circuit Court)
escalation.deadline: inside 30 days of the BZA's original final decision; no source read says a rehearing request extends the 30-day court deadline, so file in court within 30 days as well (see caveats)

escalation.trigger: You disagree with the BZA's decision (a variance granted or denied, or an appeal decided); neighbors and other aggrieved persons, aggrieved taxpayers and County bodies may also seek review
escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court: a petition styled '[Petitioner v. Respondent] In Re: [date] Decision of the Board of Zoning Appeals of [locality name]', filed with the Clerk and served on the necessary parties (the Board of Supervisors, the applicant and any different landowner of record) and the BZA's secretary
escalation.deadline: 30 days after the final decision of the board, which is the date of its final vote on the merits (mandatory and jurisdictional); serve the petition within 30 days after filing; failure to file and serve in time results in dismissal
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 15.2-2314(A), (D); BZA Rules of Procedure, Rule 6(A)
escalation.quote: Such 30-day filing requirement shall be mandatory and jurisdictional.

escalation.trigger: You disagree with the Circuit Court's final order
escalation.next: Court of Appeals of Virginia (notice of appeal)
escalation.deadline: 30 days from the date of the final judgment order (the Court of Appeals may grant an extension on motion for good cause shown)
escalation.quote: a notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals in any case within the jurisdiction of the court shall be filed within 30 days from the date of any final judgment order, decree, or conviction

escalation.trigger: What you need is a different use or a change to the rules, which a variance cannot give
escalation.next: Board of Supervisors, through a zoning map amendment (rezoning), special use permit, special exception or zoning text amendment filed with Community Development
escalation.quote: It shall not include a change in use, which change shall be accomplished by a rezoning or by a conditional zoning.

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

Local ordinance: the Zoning Ordinance (County Code Chapter 18, including § 18-34.1, which the BZA rules cite as their authority) is published on Municode, whose terms forbid automated access, and no County-hosted copy of Chapter 18 was found. It was not read and no County Code text is quoted. So these were not confirmed: the County's own variance and appeal sections; whether it bars re-filing substantially the same application for a period (Va. Code § 15.2-2310 allows up to one year); whether it lets the Zoning Administrator grant modifications under Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4) (which would bar a variance for the same relief); and which special exceptions it authorizes.

Civic Access: the portal was not opened; no account was created and nothing was filed. The County Variance page's 'Variance' link goes to #/plan/apply/124/0/0, but the Special Exceptions page (2026-04 capture) uses the same number for 'Exception or Variation – Road Plans', so one of the two links is probably wrong. Pick the Variance application type in the portal, or ask Application Services. The upload list in the portal, and whether paper or emailed applications are accepted, were not confirmed.

Fees: amounts come from the fee page capture of 2026-08-20. The Board of Supervisors held the public hearing on an amended fee schedule (County Code Chapter 1, Article 5, including § 1-504, Zoning Fees) as matter 26-220 (its Legistar history shows only a deferral on April 15, 2026 to April 22), and on April 22, 2026 it adopted the ordinance 'as presented in Attachment B' under matter 26-256 (the budget adoption item). Both agenda texts say the revised fees would take effect January 1, 2027. The new amounts have not been checked. Check the live fee page for anything filed on or after January 1, 2027.

Fees not stated plainly: the fee page does not say whether the 'Required Notice' row ($235 base plus postage and advertising) is charged on variance applications or on appeals. It sits in the zoning table, variances require newspaper and mailed notice, and Va. Code § 15.2-2204(B) charges notice costs to the applicant, so it probably applies to variances. For appeals, Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A) caps the fee at advertising and reasonable costs. The 4% technology surcharge applies to 'each fee' except required notices under Chapters 14 and 18, so it probably applies to the $590, $350 and $220 fees. No refund rule, and no BZA deferral fee, was found. Circuit court filing costs are not covered here.

Notice: the County says staff mail notice to abutting owners and publish it in the newspaper. The Public Notice Signs page says signs are posted for variances and appeals, but not who posts them or when. Va. Code § 15.2-2204(A) (published twice, the first no more than 28 days and the second at least five days before) is written for plans and ordinances and applies to BZA hearings through the cross-references in §§ 15.2-2309 and 15.2-2312. The BZA schedule's two Thursday advertisement dates fit those limits.

Owner notice when the applicant is not the owner: the County certification form lists zoning administrator determinations or appeals (and other zoning and building applications), but not variances. Va. Code § 15.2-2204(H) covers requests to the zoning administrator or the BZA that are subject to §§ 15.2-2311 or 15.2-2314. Whether the County wants the form with a tenant's variance application was not confirmed. The form says 'if the application is not the owner' as printed (the quote keeps it).
The Determinations and Appeals page (2026-05 capture) lists 'Regulations pertaining to the filing of an appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals' under Resources, with no link, so it was not read.

Missed 90-day deadlines: Va. Code §§ 15.2-2286(A)(4) and 15.2-2312 give the Zoning Administrator and the BZA 90 days, but the sources read give no remedy if either misses it (for example, whether silence can be appealed or enforced in court). So no escalation rung is listed for it; follow up in writing with Community Development and get legal advice.

Rehearing and the court deadline: the BZA rules allow a written rehearing application within 30 days, but the BZA can grant one only if the decision has not already been appealed to the Circuit Court. The 30-day court deadline in Va. Code § 15.2-2314(A) runs from the final decision, which Rule 6(A) defines as the date of the final vote, and no source read says a rehearing request pauses it. To keep court review open, file the court petition within 30 days whatever happens with a rehearing.

The County page mentions the shorter 10-day appeal period only for temporary or seasonal commercial uses. State law also allows 10 to 30 days for some other short-term, recurring violations (for example parking commercial trucks in residential districts or occupancy limits). Whether the County ordinance sets shorter periods for those was not confirmed; read the appeal statement on the notice itself.

Code versions: the index marks Va. Code §§ 15.2-2201 and 15.2-2286 'effective until January 1, 2027' and holds no successor text. Recheck the variance definition and the zoning administrator provisions on or after that date. Va. Code § 15.2-2314 in the index includes a 2026 amendment (2026, c. 368); its text is quoted as the index has it.
Court of Appeals: the Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia (Part 5A), which say where and how a notice of appeal is filed, are not in the index and were not read.

Meeting dates: from the BZA page (2026-05 capture) and the 2026 schedule. Meetings are held only when cases are scheduled and may be cancelled; the November 2026 meeting is on Tuesday Nov 10, and the 2027 dates are tentative. The variance filing deadlines do not apply to appeals.

Privacy: the County pages name the Zoning Administrator, the Deputy Zoning Administrator, the BZA staff liaisons and a notice-sign contact, with personal mailboxes and an extension. The BZA roster page names members. The FY2025 BZA annual report names members, applicants and property owners. None of these are recorded; only office lines, the cddinquiry and applicationservices role mailboxes, portals and office pages are kept. The annual report is background only and is not quoted.
Town of Scottsville: properties inside the town may fall under the town's own zoning ordinance and board of zoning appeals. Not covered here.

Special exceptions and the variance bar: Va. Code § 15.2-2309(2)(v) bars a variance when the relief is available through 'a special exception process that is authorized in the ordinance pursuant to subdivision 6 of § 15.2-2309' (the BZA's special exceptions; § 15.2-2201 defines a special exception as a special use) or through a zoning administrator modification under § 15.2-2286(A)(4). Albemarle's own 'special exceptions' waive or modify a zoning rule where the ordinance allows it, with Board of Supervisors approval. Whether those count under clause (v) was not determined, and the County Code (Chapter 18, §§ 3.1 and 33.9, which the County page links on Municode) was not read. Steps s1 and s3 say to ask Community Development.

corrections: Quotes: all 104 original quotes were checked. The 76 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised), and their subsection labels match the text; lexflow's own matcher (places.check_quotes) also matched all of them. The 28 County quotes were matched word for word against Internet Archive copies of the cited albemarle.org pages and PDFs (Variances 2026-05-12, Determinations and Appeals 2026-05-12, Board of Zoning Appeals 2026-05-15, Community Development Fees 2026-08-20, Property Inquiry 2026-03-11, BZA Rules of Procedure 2026-05-21, 2026 Submission and Review Schedule 2026-05-17, In-Person Meeting Guidelines 2026-05-18, owner-notice certification 2026-05-16), re-fetched on 2026-10-11 because www.albemarle.org still answers HTTP 403, robots.txt included. The fee-ordinance quote was matched against the Legistar Web API text of matter 26-220 (text 8668) and of matter 26-256 (text 8705). Five quotes were added and checked the same way: § 15.2-2201 (need not shared generally; not contrary to the purpose of the ordinance), § 15.2-2308.1(A) (a party who discusses facts or law ex parte must tell the other party), § 15.2-2309(1) (changing the order of evidence is reversible error only after an objection), § 15.2-2204(H) (the Zoning Administrator may direct the applicant to give the owner notice and show evidence of it) and BZA Rule 5(D) (a tie vote defeats the motion).

s1 and s3: the draft said a variance is barred whenever the relief is available as a special exception, pointing to the County's Special Exceptions page. Va. Code § 15.2-2309(2)(v) names a special exception process authorized under § 15.2-2309(6) or a zoning administrator modification under § 15.2-2286(A)(4), and the County's pages call its own Board of Supervisors special exceptions a different process from a variance. The steps now give the statute's terms and say to ask Community Development; a caveat explains the open question.

s3: the state test left out the § 15.2-2201 definition, which § 15.2-2309(2) makes part of the applicant's burden (the need must not be shared generally by other properties, and the variance must not be contrary to the purpose of the ordinance). Added.

s4: § 15.2-2204(H) puts the owner notice on the Zoning Administrator, who may direct the applicant to give it and to provide satisfactory evidence. The step now says so; the County form is that evidence.

s5: 'about nine weeks' is now 'eight to ten weeks' (the 2026 schedule's gaps run 57 to 71 days), and the example deadlines start with the next one (Nov 02, 2026); the Oct 05, 2026 deadline has passed. Row pairings were re-read from the schedule PDF in raw text order.

s6: the draft said Community Development issues an invoice payable by invoice number. The County pages only link a payment portal (whose page is the portal's invoice-payment page); the step now says that and makes the Required Notice charge conditional, as the fee caveat already did.
s8: notes that § 15.2-2309(2) also refers to property immediately across the street or road, beside the County's 'abutting parcel owners'.

s9: the draft said you may talk with BZA members 'only about procedure' and that materials 'must also be given' to the applicant. § 15.2-2308.1 says you may have ex parte communications but may not discuss the facts or law of the case, that the party who did must tell the other party and its substance, and that materials must be 'made available without cost' to the applicant, appellant or other person aggrieved. Reworded to match.
s12: adds BZA Rules 5(D) and 5(E): a tie vote defeats the motion, and defeat of a motion to deny is not approval.

s13: the draft said an appeal lies only from a written decision. § 15.2-2311(A) and § 15.2-2309(1) cover any order, requirement, decision or determination; the step now says that, and explains why a written decision still matters (a clear date, and § 15.2-2311(C) protects only written decisions).
s16: notice for an appeal hearing is now tied to §§ 15.2-2204 and 15.2-2309(3) and the County's Public Notice Signs page, not only to the variance step.
s17: adds the § 15.2-2309(1) rule that changing the order of evidence is reversible error only if the appellant objects citing that section and the board refuses to reorder.

Escalation: rung 3 (60-day protection) now uses the statute's terms ('materially changed his position in good faith reliance') and its exceptions (malfeasance, fraud, clerical corrections with the County Attorney's concurrence). Rung 4 (tie vote): the draft's 'ask at the meeting' was presented as a deadline; neither § 15.2-2311(D) nor Rule 5 sets one, and the rung now says so. Rung 6 (rehearing): the draft said a rehearing 'does not extend' the court deadline; no source says either way, so it now says no source read says it does, and to file in court within 30 days anyway. Rung 7: adds that failure to file and serve in time results in dismissal (§ 15.2-2314(A)). Rung 8: adds that the Court of Appeals may extend the time on motion for good cause (§ 8.01-675.3).

Fees: the caveat said the Board of Supervisors adopted the fee ordinance on April 22, 2026, citing matter 26-220. That matter's Legistar record shows only a public hearing and an April 15 deferral; the adoption is recorded under matter 26-256 (April 22, 2026 event item: adopt the Proposed Ordinance: Chapter 1, Article 5 (Fee Schedule) as presented in Attachment B). The caveat, the § 1-504 citation and the sources now say so. The $590, $350 and $220 fee lines in s5, s13, s15 and the fees table are now dated to the 2026-08 fee page, with the January 1, 2027 change noted. The summary now says the notice charge probably applies, not that it does.

Checked and unchanged: the five-member board appointed by the Circuit Court; meetings on the first Tuesday at 2 pm in Lane Auditorium (Nov 10 for November 2026); 15 minutes plus 5 for rebuttal and 3 minutes per public speaker (Rule 3(C)); three affirmative votes to grant a variance or reverse (Rules 5(A)(1) and (2), § 15.2-2312); roll-call votes (Rule 5(C)); 30-day rehearing application (Rule 5(J)); final decision is the date of the final vote (Rule 6(A)); the 10-day period for temporary or seasonal commercial uses as the County page words it; the 90-day limits in §§ 15.2-2286(A)(4) and 15.2-2312; the stay and restraining order in § 15.2-2311(B); the County fee rows ($590, $350, $220, $235 plus postage and advertising, 4% surcharge); the Civic Access link numbers (124, 151, 152, 206) against the pages that link them; the Circuit Court Clerk's office hours, phone lines and address on vacourts.gov.

Privacy and schema: the only mailboxes are cddinquiry@ and applicationservices@, each found as a mailto link on the County page that publishes it as the department's or Application Services' address. No staff names, personal mailboxes or direct lines are recorded (the County pages name the Zoning Administrator, the deputy, BZA liaisons, a notice-sign contact with an extension and planning staff; the court page names the elected Clerk; the Legistar records name staff and supervisors; none are kept). The JSON is valid, step and form ids are unique, every step's form id exists, and the category is in the schema.

legal_basis[73]: the sentence 'If adopted, the revised fees would take effect January 1, 2027' is in the matter's agenda text (the Legistar API's texts resource for matter 26-220, version 1), not in the matter record itself; the citation now names that resource.
open_issues: www.albemarle.org answers this client with HTTP 403, robots.txt included (checked again 2026-10-11). Every County quote was confirmed against an Internet Archive copy of the cited official URL, not the live page. Re-check against the live pages when they can be read.

The Zoning Ordinance (County Code Chapter 18) was not read: Municode's terms forbid automated access and no County-hosted copy was found. Not confirmed: whether the County authorizes zoning administrator modifications under § 15.2-2286(A)(4), whether its Board of Supervisors special exceptions count under § 15.2-2309(2)(v), any one-year bar on refiling, and the County's own variance and appeal sections. Steps s1 and s3 tell the user to ask Community Development.

The revised fee amounts that take effect January 1, 2027 were not read (the ordinance is an attachment on albemarle.legistar1.com, whose robots.txt disallows all agents). The fee lines are dated; anything filed on or after January 1, 2027 needs the live fee page.

Whether the Required Notice charge ($235 plus postage and advertising) is billed on variances, appeals or both, and whether the owner-notice certification is wanted with a tenant's variance application, are not stated on the County pages; both are marked as unconfirmed in the steps and caveats.

The County Variance page's Civic Access link (#/plan/apply/124/0/0) is the same number the Special Exceptions page uses for 'Exception or Variation – Road Plans'; the form entry points to the portal home instead. Not resolved.
Whether a BZA rehearing request pauses the 30-day court deadline in § 15.2-2314(A) is not settled by any source read; the file advises filing in court within 30 days regardless.
Not researched: the Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia (Part 5A) for the Court of Appeals step, circuit court filing costs, and the Town of Scottsville's own zoning and board of zoning appeals.
The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting site content; the quotes are one sentence or clause each, with citations. Whether publishing them needs permission is the project owner's decision.
